question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Cities and the formation of the English East India Company in 1600]
options: London — City where the founding merchants of the EIC were primarily based
Leadenhall Street, London — Street where the EIC's headquarters (India House) was eventually located
Plymouth — Port from which the first EIC fleet under James Lancaster departed in 1601
Lisbon — City whose merchants' monopoly on spice trade the EIC's charter aimed to challenge
wrong_fact: The first EIC fleet did NOT depart from Plymouth. It set sail from Woolwich (near London) on the River Thames in February 1601. Plymouth is associated with Francis Drake's 1577 circumnavigation, not the EIC's first voyage.
explanation: The EIC was formed by London merchants and its headquarters ultimately settled on Leadenhall Street. Lisbon (Portugal) dominated the Eastern spice trade that the EIC challenged. The first fleet under James Lancaster sailed from Woolwich on the Thames — not Plymouth, which was Drake's and Hawkins' home port.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European trading companies and their founding cities/countries]
options: English East India Company (1600) — London, England
Dutch East India Company / VOC (1602) — Amsterdam, Netherlands
French East India Company / Compagnie des Indes Orientales (1664) — Paris/Lorient, France
Danish East India Company (1616) — Copenhagen, Denmark — preceded the English EIC by 16 years
wrong_fact: The Danish East India Company (1616) did NOT precede the English EIC. The English EIC was founded in 1600, 16 years BEFORE the Danish company was established in 1616. The claim is reversed.
explanation: The sequence of European East India Companies: English EIC (1600), Dutch VOC (1602), Danish (1616), Portuguese Estado da India (formal charter earlier but reorganised later), French (1664). The EIC was the earliest among these. Copenhagen was indeed the base of the Danish East India Company.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Regional origin of founding EIC investors/merchants and their geographical trade connections]
options: Levant Company merchants — Many founding EIC shareholders came from this London-based company trading in the Eastern Mediterranean (Istanbul, Aleppo, Alexandria)
Bristol — Major English port whose merchants dominated the initial EIC share subscription in 1599
Middelburg (Netherlands) — Site of a failed joint Anglo-Dutch spice venture that preceded the EIC
Muscovy Company — Another London trading company whose model influenced the EIC's joint-stock structure
wrong_fact: Bristol merchants did NOT dominate the initial EIC share subscription. The EIC was predominantly a London enterprise; the 1599 subscription drive was led by London merchants, and the company was formally a London-centred institution. Bristol merchants were more associated with Atlantic trade.
explanation: The EIC grew from a 1599 meeting of London merchants, many of whom were members of the Levant Company. The Muscovy Company (est. 1555) provided an organisational model. A joint Anglo-Dutch venture had been discussed at Middelburg before the EIC received its charter. Bristol was an important English port but its merchants were not the driving force behind EIC formation — London Levant Company merchants were.
